content: Important Notes: While using this medication, it is essential to undergo regular laboratory and/or medical tests, such as eye examinations. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. To minimize the risk of transmitting HIV to others, always use an effective barrier method, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity. Missed Dose Instructions: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose of cidofovir, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. If you miss a dose of probenecid, inform your doctor or pharmacist right away. Storage Guidelines: Refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist for specific storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Usage Information: This medication is administered via intravenous injection, as directed by your doctor, typically every 1 to 2 weeks. The injection is given slowly over the course of one hour. It must not be injected into the eyes. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, body weight, and response to treatment. Intravenous fluids are usually given before the cidofovir dose. Additionally, your doctor will instruct you to take probenecid orally before and after receiving cidofovir. To prevent kidney problems, drink plenty of fluids unless otherwise directed by your doctor. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you are thoroughly trained by your healthcare professional on preparation and usage. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. Probenecid Use: It is critical to use probenecid exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Taking probenecid after meals may help prevent nausea and vomiting. This medication works best when used consistently and regularly. Do not alter the prescribed dosage or stop using it (or your HIV medications) without your doctor’s approval. Precautions: Avoid direct contact of this medication with your skin, eyes, or mouth. If contact occurs, wash thoroughly with soap and water. Inform your doctor if you are allergic to cidofovir, other antivirals (e.g., ganciclovir), probenecid, sulfa drugs (e.g., sulfamethoxazole), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This drug may cause vision changes. Do not drive, operate machinery, or perform tasks requiring clear vision until you are confident you can do so safely. During pregnancy, cidofovir should only be used when absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. The manufacturer advises avoiding pregnancy during treatment. Men with female partners should use effective barrier protection (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms) during all sexual activity while on this medication and for at least 90 days after stopping it. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. If you have HIV, breastfeeding is not recommended as breast milk can transmit the virus. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Avoid taking other medications that may harm your kidneys (e.g., amphotericin B, foscarnet, pentamidine, vancomycin, aminoglycosides like tobramycin, or NSAIDs like ibuprofen) within 7 days before and during treatment with this medication. Serious, potentially fatal kidney damage may occur in some cases. Check the labels of all your medications for NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen). Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Side Effects: Nausea, headache, and vomiting may occur, particularly with probenecid use. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor for medical advice. Final Notes: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
